text_blocks.snippet: Residents in Central Illinois face an increase in targeted scams involving artificial intelligence, phishing, and local impersonations.
snippet_highlighted_words: artificial intelligence, phishing, and local impersonations

list.snippet: AI Voice & Phone Scams: Scammers use artificial intelligence to clone voices or make fake phone calls sound realistic, often targeting residents in areas like Peoria and surrounding counties. Central Illinois banks and the Peoria County Sheriff’s Office have issued warnings about a rise in these calls .

Peoria County Jail / Bail Scams: Fraudsters pose as a Sergeant or Captain with the Sheriff’s Office, claiming a family member is detained and demanding bail money through peer-to-peer apps like Zelle under the false claim that computers are down.

State Agency & Tollway Phishing: Scammers send fake texts, emails, and calls impersonating Illinois state departments, the Illinois Secretary of State’s office, or the Illinois Tollway. These messages often claim there is a violation or demand payment within 12 hours under threat of arrest.

Municipal & Permit Impersonation: Local entities (such as warnings issued around Wilmette and Central Illinois municipalities) report fake emails sent to homeowners and businesses requesting wire transfers for permit or utility fees using forged department logos.

Romance & Social Media Shopping Scams: Fraudsters build fake online relationships to swindles victims out of thousands of dollars, or run social media ads featuring deep discounts on trending items that never ship.
Urgent Demands: Scammers create a false sense of emergency (e.g., "pay within 12 hours" or "your loved one is in jail").
Unusual Payment Methods: Requests to pay via Zelle, cryptocurrency, gift cards, wire transfers, or prepaid cards.

Unsolicited Links: Texts or emails containing links claiming to be from state agencies or toll authorities. Official state offices will not ask for Social Security numbers or private banking data via text or email.

text_blocks.snippet: What You Should Do / How to Report

list.snippet: Hang Up and Verify: Do not call back numbers provided in suspicious texts or emails. Look up the official phone number of the agency, bank, or sheriff’s office independently.
Establish a Safe Word: Families are advised by local authorities to set up a private safe word to verify identity during unexpected phone calls involving money.
Contact your local police department or county sheriff to file a fraud report .
Call the Illinois Attorney General’s Consumer Fraud Hotline at 800-386-5438.
Review federal guidance and file complaints via the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) or check resources provided through University of Illinois Extension Guide .
